subject.title: Durable core PR2/6: add optional shared-state foundation

question: Should OpenClaw own a shared durable residual schema in `state/openclaw.sqlite` before any approved runtime consumer needs it?
rationale: The implementation is internally coherent, but deciding whether cross-owner execution, wake, delivery-evidence, and uncertainty facts belong in core rather than existing owner-specific stores is a product and architecture choice that code review cannot safely infer.

options.title: Defer implementation pending RFC approval
options.body: Keep this PR open behind the RFC gate and require explicit sponsorship of the shared durable boundary before further core storage work lands.

options.title: Sponsor a narrowed core foundation
options.body: Approve only a named residual fact set, then require a current-main rebase and fresh-install plus upgrade proof for the approved tables and lease lifecycle.

options.title: Keep these facts owner-specific
options.body: Reject the shared layer and route each demonstrated recovery or delivery gap to its existing task, flow, subagent, session, or outbound-delivery owner.

recommendation.title: Defer implementation pending RFC approval
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open behind the RFC gate and require explicit sponsorship of the shared durable boundary before further core storage work lands.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest visible context for the RFC and implementation series, while the final product decision remains with an OpenClaw core owner.
